Superhero Intelligence System¶

Can six ability scores tell a hero from a villain?

Sections: 2 Data Preparation · Task 1 Classification · Task 2 Clustering · Task 3 Neural Network

import numpy as np, pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

SEED = 42
np.random.seed(SEED)

SCORES = ["intelligence_score", "strength_score", "speed_score",
          "durability_score", "power_score", "combat_score"]
COLORS = {"hero": "#1F5FBF", "villain": "#D62839", "baseline": "#9E9E9E",
          "tree": "#2E7D32", "knn": "#F9A825", "netA": "#6A1B9A", "netB": "#00838F"}

Section 2: Data Preparation¶

Step 1: Inspect (T1)¶

In [2]:
train_raw = pd.read_csv("data/train.csv")
test_raw = pd.read_csv("data/test.csv")

def inspect(df, label):
    print(f"== {label}: shape {df.shape}")
    use = SCORES + ["alignment", "name"]
    num = df[SCORES].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = pd.DataFrame({
        "dtype": df[use].dtypes.astype(str),
        "missing": df[use].isna().sum(),
        "zeros": [(num[c] == 0).sum() if c in SCORES else np.nan for c in use],
    })
    # blanks/non-numeric that become NaN + zeros that become NaN
    t["-> NaN (total)"] = [num[c].isna().sum() + (num[c] == 0).sum() if c in SCORES else np.nan for c in use]
    display(t)

print("Columns:", list(train_raw.columns))
inspect(train_raw, "train.csv"); inspect(test_raw, "test.csv")

Steps 2-4: duplicates, mark missing, drop weak rows (T2)¶

In [3]:
n = {"Loaded": (len(train_raw), len(test_raw))}
cols = ["name", "alignment"] + SCORES
train, test = train_raw[cols].copy(), test_raw[cols].copy()

# Step 2: duplicates
train = train.drop_duplicates("name", keep="first")
test = test.drop_duplicates("name", keep="first")
train = train[~train["name"].isin(test["name"])]
n["After step 2 (duplicates)"] = (len(train), len(test))

# Step 3: blanks and 0 -> NaN
def mark_missing(df):
    df = df.copy()
    df[SCORES] = df[SCORES].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").replace(0, np.nan)
    return df
train, test = mark_missing(train), mark_missing(test)

# Step 4: drop rows with 3+ missing scores
train = train[train[SCORES].isna().sum(axis=1) < 3]
test = test[test[SCORES].isna().sum(axis=1) < 3]
n["After step 4 (weak rows)"] = (len(train), len(test))

Clean Set A (clustering) and Clean Set B (classification / NN)¶

In [4]:
set_a = train.reset_index(drop=True)                      # Task 2: all characters, train only

def set_b(df):
    df = df[df["alignment"].isin(["Good", "Bad"])].copy()
    df["target"] = df["alignment"].map({"Good": 0, "Bad": 1})
    return df.reset_index(drop=True)
train_b, test_b = set_b(train), set_b(test)               # Tasks 1 & 3

n["Clean Set A"] = (len(set_a), "not used")
n["Clean Set B"] = (len(train_b), len(test_b))

      "| test", len(test) - len(test_b))

Task 1: Classification (25 marks)¶

Baseline, Decision Tree, KNN on Clean Set B. Test once at the end.

Class balance (T3, G1)¶

In [5]:
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.dummy import DummyClassifier
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV, StratifiedKFold
from sklearn.metrics import (classification_report, confusion_matrix,
                             precision_recall_fscore_support, accuracy_score, f1_score)
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap

X_tr, y_tr = train_b[SCORES], train_b["target"]
X_te, y_te = test_b[SCORES], test_b["target"]

counts = pd.DataFrame({"train.csv": train_b["alignment"].value_counts(),
                       "test.csv": test_b["alignment"].value_counts()}).loc[["Good", "Bad"]]
T3 = counts.join((counts / counts.sum() * 100).round(1).add_suffix(" %"))
print("T3: Class counts and % in each file"); display(T3)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
w = 0.35
for j, (cls, col) in enumerate([("Good", COLORS["hero"]), ("Bad", COLORS["villain"])]):
    bars = ax.bar(np.arange(2) + (j - 0.5) * w, counts.loc[cls], w, color=col, label=f"{cls} ({'Hero' if cls=='Good' else 'Villain'})")
    for b, v, tot in zip(bars, counts.loc[cls], counts.sum()):
        ax.text(b.get_x() + w / 2, b.get_height() + 5, f"{v}\n{v/tot:.1%}", ha="center", fontsize=9)
ax.set_xticks(range(2)); ax.set_xticklabels(counts.columns)
ax.set_ylim(0, counts.values.max() * 1.2)
ax.set_xlabel("File"); ax.set_ylabel("Characters"); ax.set_title("G1: Class counts (Clean Set B)"); ax.legend()
plt.show()

Models and grid search (T4)¶

In [6]:
cv = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=SEED)
median = lambda: SimpleImputer(strategy="median")

baseline = DummyClassifier(strategy="most_frequent").fit(X_tr, y_tr)

tree_gs = GridSearchCV(
    Pipeline([("imputer", median()), ("model", DecisionTreeClassifier(criterion="gini", random_state=SEED))]),
    {"model__max_depth": [3, 5, 7, 10, None], "model__min_samples_leaf": [1, 5, 10]},
    cv=cv, scoring="f1_macro", refit=True)
knn_gs = GridSearchCV(
    Pipeline([("imputer", median()), ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
              ("model", KNeighborsClassifier(metric="euclidean"))]),
    {"model__n_neighbors": [3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 15], "model__weights": ["uniform", "distance"]},
    cv=cv, scoring="f1_macro", refit=True)
tree_gs.fit(X_tr, y_tr); knn_gs.fit(X_tr, y_tr)

T4 = pd.DataFrame({
    "Model": ["Decision Tree", "KNN"],
    "Best settings": [{k.split("__")[1]: v for k, v in g.best_params_.items()} for g in (tree_gs, knn_gs)],
    "Best CV macro-F1": [round(g.best_score_, 3) for g in (tree_gs, knn_gs)]})
print("T4: Best settings and best CV macro-F1"); display(T4)

Test once (T5)¶

In [7]:
models = {"Baseline": baseline, "Decision Tree": tree_gs.best_estimator_, "KNN": knn_gs.best_estimator_}
MODEL_COLORS = {"Baseline": COLORS["baseline"], "Decision Tree": COLORS["tree"], "KNN": COLORS["knn"]}

def evaluate(m):
    p = m.predict(X_te)
    (ph, pv), (rh, rv), (fh, fv), _ = precision_recall_fscore_support(y_te, p, labels=[0, 1], zero_division=0)
    return {"Train Macro-F1": f1_score(y_tr, m.predict(X_tr), average="macro"),
            "Accuracy": accuracy_score(y_te, p),
            "Precision Hero": ph, "Recall Hero": rh, "F1 Hero": fh,
            "Precision Villain": pv, "Recall Villain": rv, "F1 Villain": fv,
            "Macro-F1": f1_score(y_te, p, average="macro"),
            "Macro-Precision": (ph + pv) / 2, "Macro-Recall": (rh + rv) / 2}

T5_full = pd.DataFrame({k: evaluate(m) for k, m in models.items()}).T
T5 = T5_full.drop(columns=["Macro-Precision", "Macro-Recall"])
print("T5: Task 1 results (test.csv, except Train Macro-F1)"); display(T5.round(3))
for k, m in models.items():
    print(f"--- {k}"); print(classification_report(y_te, m.predict(X_te), target_names=["Hero", "Villain"], digits=3, zero_division=0))

Confusion matrices (G2, G3)¶

In [8]:
def plot_cm(ax, model, name, color):
    cm = confusion_matrix(y_te, model.predict(X_te), labels=[0, 1])
    ax.imshow(cm, cmap=LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("c", ["white", color]))
    for (r, c), v in np.ndenumerate(cm):
        ax.text(c, r, v, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=14, color="white" if v > cm.max() / 2 else "black")
    ax.set_xticks([0, 1]); ax.set_xticklabels(["Good", "Bad"]); ax.set_yticks([0, 1]); ax.set_yticklabels(["Good", "Bad"])
    ax.set_xlabel("Predicted"); ax.set_ylabel("Actual"); ax.set_title(name)
    return cm

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4, 3.6)); cm_tree = plot_cm(ax, models["Decision Tree"], "G2: Confusion matrix, Decision Tree (test)", COLORS["tree"]); plt.show()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4, 3.6)); cm_knn = plot_cm(ax, models["KNN"], "G3: Confusion matrix, KNN (test)", COLORS["knn"]); plt.show()

Winner by the rules¶

In [10]:
t, k, b = (T5_full.loc[n] for n in ["Decision Tree", "KNN", "Baseline"])
if abs(t["Macro-F1"] - k["Macro-F1"]) < 0.01:
    winner = "Decision Tree" if t["Recall Villain"] >= k["Recall Villain"] else "KNN"; rule = "tie-break on Villain recall"
else:
    winner = "Decision Tree" if t["Macro-F1"] > k["Macro-F1"] else "KNN"; rule = "highest test Macro-F1"
print(f"Winner: {winner} ({rule})")
for n in ["Decision Tree", "KNN"]:
    r = T5_full.loc[n]
    print(f"{n}: beats baseline by {r['Macro-F1'] - b['Macro-F1']:+.3f} | train-test gap {r['Train Macro-F1'] - r['Macro-F1']:.3f}"
          f" -> {'overfits' if r['Train Macro-F1'] - r['Macro-F1'] > 0.10 else 'no overfit flag'}")

Winner: KNN (highest test Macro-F1)
Decision Tree: beats baseline by +0.030 | train-test gap 0.155 -> overfits
KNN: beats baseline by +0.148 | train-test gap 0.213 -> overfits

Task 1 answers¶

Q1. KNN wins: test Macro-F1 0.526 vs 0.408 for the Decision Tree (gap well above 0.01, so no tie-break). Best settings: KNN k=3, uniform weights; Tree max_depth=5, min_samples_leaf=10.

Q2. Both beat the Baseline (0.378) on Macro-F1, but by very different margins: KNN by +0.148, the Decision Tree by only +0.030. The Baseline's 0.609 accuracy is just the Hero share of test; it never finds a villain. Both models have lower accuracy than the Baseline (0.573 and 0.560), which is the price of trying to catch villains.

Q3. Villains are harder. Decision Tree: 6 of 88 villains caught (recall 0.068), 82 missed. KNN: 29 of 88 caught (recall 0.330), 59 missed. Heroes are recalled far better (0.876 and 0.730). The models lean towards predicting Hero because it is the majority class.

Q4. Both overfit by the rule (train − test Macro-F1 > 0.10): Tree 0.563 − 0.408 = 0.155, KNN 0.739 − 0.526 = 0.213. KNN with k=3 memorises the training data (its training score is inflated because each point is its own nearest neighbour). Note the best CV macro-F1 scores (0.540 and 0.517) are close to the test scores, so the weak performance is real, not just an overfitting artefact: the 6 scores carry little signal about alignment.

Task 2: Clustering (25 marks)¶

K-Means and Agglomerative on Clean Set A. alignment only looked at after clustering.

Fill, scale and choose k (G5, G6)¶

In [11]:
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans, AgglomerativeClustering
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.metrics import silhouette_score, davies_bouldin_score, calinski_harabasz_score, adjusted_rand_score
from scipy.cluster.hierarchy import linkage, dendrogram

prep = Pipeline([("imputer", median()), ("scaler", StandardScaler())])
X_s = prep.fit_transform(set_a[SCORES])          # fitted on Clean Set A; alignment never used

ks = list(range(2, 9))
km_fits = {k: KMeans(n_clusters=k, n_init=10, random_state=SEED).fit(X_s) for k in ks}
inertia = [km_fits[k].inertia_ for k in ks]
sil = [silhouette_score(X_s, km_fits[k].labels_) for k in ks]
best_k = ks[int(np.argmax(np.round(sil, 3)))]     # ties (3 decimals) -> smaller k (argmax takes the first)
display(pd.DataFrame({"k": ks, "inertia": np.round(inertia, 1), "silhouette": np.round(sil, 3)}).set_index("k").T)
print("Final k =", best_k)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.8))
ax.plot(ks, inertia, "o-", color="#444444"); ax.axvline(best_k, ls="--", color="grey", label=f"chosen k = {best_k}")
ax.set_xlabel("k (number of clusters)"); ax.set_ylabel("Inertia"); ax.set_title("G5: Elbow curve (K-Means)"); ax.legend(); plt.show()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.8))
ax.plot(ks, sil, "o-", color="#444444"); ax.plot(best_k, sil[ks.index(best_k)], "o", ms=12, color="#D62839", label=f"final k = {best_k}")
ax.set_xlabel("k (number of clusters)"); ax.set_ylabel("Silhouette score"); ax.set_title("G6: Silhouette score vs k"); ax.legend(); plt.show()

Dendrogram (G7)¶

In [12]:
Z = linkage(X_s, method="ward")
n_pts = len(X_s)
cut = (Z[n_pts - best_k - 1, 2] + Z[n_pts - best_k, 2]) / 2     # height between the merges that leave k and k-1 groups
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4.5))
dendrogram(Z, truncate_mode="lastp", p=30, ax=ax, color_threshold=0, above_threshold_color="#555555")
ax.axhline(cut, ls="--", color="#D62839", label=f"cut at k = {best_k}")
ax.set_xlabel("Cluster (leaf size in brackets)"); ax.set_ylabel("Ward distance"); ax.set_title("G7: Dendrogram (Ward, last 30 merges)"); ax.legend(); plt.show()

Both algorithms, metrics and renumbering (T6)¶

In [13]:
km_raw = km_fits[best_k].labels_
ag_raw = AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=best_k, linkage="ward").fit_predict(X_s)

def scores(l): return silhouette_score(X_s, l), davies_bouldin_score(X_s, l), calinski_harabasz_score(X_s, l)
m_km, m_ag = scores(km_raw), scores(ag_raw)
wins_km = int(m_km[0] > m_ag[0]) + int(m_km[1] < m_ag[1]) + int(m_km[2] > m_ag[2])
ari = adjusted_rand_score(km_raw, ag_raw)
T6 = pd.DataFrame([["K-Means", best_k, *m_km, wins_km], ["Agglomerative", best_k, *m_ag, 3 - wins_km],
                   ["ARI between the two", "", ari, "", "", ""]],
                  columns=["Algorithm", "k", "Silhouette", "Davies-Bouldin", "Calinski-Harabasz", "Wins (of 3)"])
print("T6: Clustering metrics"); display(T6.round(3).set_index("Algorithm"))

def renumber(raw):
    """Cluster 1 = lowest average of the 6 scores (original 0-100 scale)."""
    order = set_a[SCORES].groupby(raw).mean().mean(axis=1).sort_values().index
    m = {old: new + 1 for new, old in enumerate(order)}
    return np.array([m[l] for l in raw])
km_lab, ag_lab = renumber(km_raw), renumber(ag_raw)

PCA scatter plots (G8, G9)¶

In [14]:
pca = PCA(n_components=2, random_state=SEED)
P = pca.fit_transform(X_s); ev = pca.explained_variance_ratio_ * 100
tab = plt.cm.tab10

def pca_scatter(labels, title):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 5))
    for c in sorted(set(labels)):
        ax.scatter(P[labels == c, 0], P[labels == c, 1], s=14, color=tab(c - 1), label=f"Cluster {c}")
    ax.set_xlabel(f"PC1 ({ev[0]:.1f}% variance)"); ax.set_ylabel(f"PC2 ({ev[1]:.1f}% variance)")
    ax.set_title(title); ax.legend(); plt.show()
pca_scatter(km_lab, "G8: PCA scatter, K-Means"); pca_scatter(ag_lab, "G9: PCA scatter, Agglomerative")

Cluster profiles (G10, G11, T7)¶

In [15]:
SHORT = ["INT", "STR", "SPD", "DUR", "POW", "COM"]
def profile(labels):
    p = set_a[SCORES].groupby(labels).mean(); p.columns = SHORT
    p.insert(0, "Size", pd.Series(labels).value_counts().sort_index().values)
    p.index.name = "Cluster"; return p
prof_km, prof_ag = profile(km_lab), profile(ag_lab)

def plot_profile(p, title):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4)); k = len(p); w = 0.8 / k
    for j, c in enumerate(p.index):
        ax.bar(np.arange(6) + (j - (k - 1) / 2) * w, p.loc[c, SHORT], w, color=tab(c - 1), label=f"Cluster {c}")
    ax.set_xticks(range(6)); ax.set_xticklabels(SHORT); ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
    ax.set_xlabel("Score"); ax.set_ylabel("Average score (0-100)"); ax.set_title(title); ax.legend(); plt.show()
plot_profile(prof_km, "G10: Cluster profiles, K-Means"); plot_profile(prof_ag, "G11: Cluster profiles, Agglomerative")

Task 2 answers¶

Q5. k = 2. It has the highest Silhouette (0.307 vs 0.221-0.240 for k = 3 to 8). The Elbow curve falls smoothly (inertia 4154 at k=2 to 2254 at k=8) with no sharp bend, only a mild flattening after k = 3-4, so it gives no clear k of its own and does not change the choice. Even the best Silhouette (0.307) is in the "weak" band (0.26-0.50); for k >= 3 it is at or below 0.25 ("no real structure"). The data form one continuum more than clearly separate groups.

Q6. Moderately similar: ARI = 0.483 (moderate band, 0.40-0.69). Both algorithms find the same two kinds of character: a lower-strength group with high intelligence and combat, and a high-all-round-power group. They differ on the border: Agglomerative's strong group is smaller (334 vs 493 characters) and more extreme (STR 84 vs 70), while K-Means puts more borderline characters into its strong group.

Q7. K-Means is better separated: it wins all 3 metrics (Silhouette 0.307 vs 0.278, Davies-Bouldin 1.274 vs 1.290, Calinski-Harabasz 586.8 vs 460.9). Interpretability is close to a tie: the average gap between the two clusters across the 6 scores is about 31 points for K-Means and 30 for Agglomerative. Agglomerative separates strength more (24 vs 84), K-Means separates speed and power more. K-Means is slightly easier by a hair, and has more balanced cluster sizes (579 / 493 vs 738 / 334).

Q8. Both algorithms give two clusters.

  • Cluster 1 (brainy tacticians / brainy fighters): high intelligence (about 85) and good combat (67-70) but low strength (20-24) and modest speed and durability. 579 characters (K-Means), 738 (Agglomerative).
  • Cluster 2 (all-round powerhouses / elite powerhouses): high on everything, with power 93-95 and durability 84-89. 493 characters (K-Means), 334 (Agglomerative).
  • Villains: no cluster is mostly villains. Good is the largest alignment in every cluster (61% / 48% for K-Means, 60% / 44% for Agglomerative). The powerhouse cluster has the most villains (34.5% K-Means, 37.7% Agglomerative) and the fewest heroes, but the difference from Cluster 1 (27%) is modest. Percentages are of all alignments, including Neutral and blank.

Build and train both networks (T9)¶

In [19]:
def build(hidden):
    tf.keras.utils.set_random_seed(SEED)
    m = tf.keras.Sequential([tf.keras.Input(shape=(6,))] +
                            [tf.keras.layers.Dense(n, activation="relu") for n in hidden] +
                            [tf.keras.layers.Dense(1, activation="sigmoid")])
    m.compile(optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=0.001), loss="binary_crossentropy")
    return m

nets, hist = {}, {}
for name, hidden in [("Network A", [8]), ("Network B", [16, 8])]:
    nets[name] = build(hidden)
    hist[name] = nets[name].fit(Xf, y_fit, validation_data=(Xv, y_val), batch_size=32, epochs=200, verbose=0,
        callbacks=[tf.keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(monitor="val_loss", patience=15, restore_best_weights=True)])

best_ep = {n: int(np.argmin(h.history["val_loss"])) + 1 for n, h in hist.items()}

Architecture diagrams (G12)¶

In [20]:
def draw_net(ax, sizes, title, color):
    xs = np.linspace(0, 1, len(sizes)); pos = []
    for x, n in zip(xs, sizes):
        ys = np.linspace(-(n - 1) / 2, (n - 1) / 2, n) * 0.1; pos.append([(x, y) for y in ys])
    for a, b in zip(pos[:-1], pos[1:]):
        for p in a:
            for q in b: ax.plot([p[0], q[0]], [p[1], q[1]], color="#CCCCCC", lw=0.4, zorder=1)
    for layer in pos: ax.scatter(*zip(*layer), s=170, color=color, edgecolor="black", zorder=2)
    labels = ["Input\n6 scores"] + [f"Hidden {i+1}\n{n} ReLU" for i, n in enumerate(sizes[1:-1])] + ["Output\n1 sigmoid"]
    for x, l in zip(xs, labels): ax.text(x, -1.0, l, ha="center", va="top", fontsize=9)
    ax.set_xlim(-0.12, 1.12); ax.set_ylim(-1.4, 0.95); ax.axis("off"); ax.set_title(title)

fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4.5))
draw_net(axs[0], [6, 8, 1], f"Network A (6-8-1, {nets['Network A'].count_params()} parameters)", COLORS["netA"])
draw_net(axs[1], [6, 16, 8, 1], f"Network B (6-16-8-1, {nets['Network B'].count_params()} parameters)", COLORS["netB"])
fig.suptitle("G12: Architecture diagrams, Network A and Network B"); plt.show()

from functools import cmp_to_key
final = {n: {"acc": T5_full.loc[n, "Accuracy"], "f1": T5_full.loc[n, "Macro-F1"], "rv": T5_full.loc[n, "Recall Villain"]} for n in models}
for name in nets:
    r = T10[(T10.Network == name) & (T10.Split == "test")].iloc[0]
    final[name] = {"acc": r["Accuracy"], "f1": r["Macro-F1"],
                   "rv": precision_recall_fscore_support(y_te, probs[name], labels=[0, 1], zero_division=0)[1][1]}

def cmp(a, b):   # higher macro-F1 first; gap under 0.01 -> higher Villain recall first
    fa, fb = final[a], final[b]
    d = fb["rv"] - fa["rv"] if abs(fa["f1"] - fb["f1"]) < 0.01 else fb["f1"] - fa["f1"]
    return int(d > 0) - int(d < 0)
order = sorted(final, key=cmp_to_key(cmp))
T11 = pd.DataFrame([[i + 1, n, final[n]["acc"], final[n]["f1"], final[n]["rv"],
                     "-" if n == "Baseline" else ("yes" if final[n]["f1"] > final["Baseline"]["f1"] else "no")]
                    for i, n in enumerate(order)],
                   columns=["Rank", "Model", "Test accuracy", "Test Macro-F1", "Villain recall", "Beats baseline?"]).set_index("Rank")
print("T11: Final ranking (test.csv)"); display(T11.round(3))

ALL_COLORS = {**MODEL_COLORS, **NET_COLORS}

    bars = ax.bar(np.arange(2) + (j - 2) * w, vals, w, color=ALL_COLORS[n], label=n)
    for b, v in zip(bars, vals): ax.text(b.get_x() + w / 2, v + 0.01, f"{v:.2f}", ha="center", fontsize=8)
ax.set_xticks(range(2)); ax.set_xticklabels(["Accuracy", "Macro-F1"]); ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
ax.set_xlabel("Metric"); ax.set_ylabel("Score (test.csv)"); ax.set_title("G16: Final comparison, all 5 models"); ax.legend(ncol=3, fontsize=8); plt.show()

Task 3 answers¶

Q9. No. Network B's test Macro-F1 (0.421) is 0.034 lower than Network A's (0.455), so the deeper network did not improve results (the bar is +0.01). With only 6 weak input features there is little extra structure for the second hidden layer to learn: B reaches a slightly lower training loss but its validation loss is worse (0.633 vs 0.621), and extra capacity mainly lets it fit noise.

Q10. Network A: training and validation loss fall together and stay close, flattening around 0.63. Best epoch 151 (stopped at 166). No overfitting; if anything the loss stays high and flat, a sign of limited learning signal (mild underfitting). Network B: validation loss bottoms out at epoch 57 (0.633) and then drifts up while training loss keeps falling, which is overfitting by the brief's rule; early stopping restored the epoch-57 weights. The train-test Macro-F1 gaps are small (A 0.039, B 0.064), under the 0.10 threshold.

Q11. Against the Decision Tree: yes on Macro-F1 (A 0.455 and B 0.421 vs 0.408), but the margins are small (+0.047 and +0.013) and come mostly from higher accuracy, since both networks predict "Hero" almost always (Villain recall 0.091 and 0.057 vs 0.068 for the tree). Against KNN: no. KNN's Macro-F1 (0.526) beats A by 0.071 and B by 0.105, and its Villain recall (0.330) is far higher. Final ranking by test Macro-F1: KNN, Network A, Network B, Decision Tree, Baseline. All four models beat the Baseline (0.378). Note that the networks learned from 80% of train.csv, the tree and KNN from 100%.

Q12. (1) Weak features: the 6 ability scores carry little information about alignment (best CV Macro-F1 is only about 0.54, test best 0.53), and about 8% of score cells were 0/blank and had to be filled with medians. Alignment is also a subjective label (Neutral, blank and Good/Bad overlap in scores), so the task has a low ceiling. (2) Small data and one split: only 916 training and 225 test characters, one fixed test set whose class mix (61/39) differs from train (64/36), single network runs without repeats, and no tuning of the networks (not allowed), so small score differences (e.g. 0.01-0.03) could be noise.
